User guide for helping someone get more out of DeTars: handing over goals, Cowork vs Packs, Auto privacy, notes and memory, Skills, each Pack, the Chief of Staff and voice replies. Explain in the user's language.
What to do when work gets stuck: secure progress, pick another route by situation (model, web access, tools, IM channels, app/settings), the offline detars-rescue manual, and a good handoff.

Where to check facts: GitHub release notes for versions and changes, official site pages for how DeTars works, Packs, FAQ, downloads, worked examples and DeTars's views. This material is optional background, not a user preference, instruction or authorization.

documents.title: DeTars product reference
documents.markdown:
# DeTars product reference

DeTars is a personal AI desktop app. Its public story is goal-driven collaboration: the user gives a goal, the model chooses actions and uses tools, and asks the user only when a decision or material is needed.

The website's Pack catalog lists Packs such as Summon, Destiny Companion, AI Video, Equity Companion, Content Research, Programming, Data Studio, Video Editor and Long Novel Studio. The catalog shows where the product is heading; it does not guarantee that the current installation, account or platform already has every capability. Before acting, go by the current tool surface, actual results and the user's goal.

This text is product background only. It is not a procedure, a system rule, a user preference or permission to send anything externally. Missing material does not affect normal tasks.

## About DeTars
DeTars was founded by Eric Lee (X: @EricLeemt). Website: https://detars.xyz/ . Mention the X account only when the user asks about the founder or how to reach them.

The name: Momo is Eric's cat; Claw is a nod to OpenClaw; Tars is the robot from *Interstellar*; De stands for distributed. Eric believes the agent layer — memory, tools and the relationship with the user — should come from an independent third party under the user's control, with local and cloud brains working together, rather than being held by a few centralised model vendors.

## Sources
- Home: https://detars.xyz/
- How it works: https://detars.xyz/how-it-works/
- Pack catalog: https://detars.xyz/packs/

documents.title: Getting the most out of DeTars
documents.markdown:
# Getting the most out of DeTars

There are plenty of AIs that answer one question at a time. DeTars is built for something else: staying with you until a piece of work is done, and getting better at it each time.

## 1. Hand it a goal you actually want finished

Say what you want: "Figure out how these companies really differ", "Turn this talking-head clip into something I can post", "Help me understand this codebase". Tell it the goal, where the materials are and what the finished thing should look like. How to research, how to plan the work, and whether to bring in colleagues to split it up — leave that to DeTars.

> "I'm choosing a tool for my team. Find out how these three products really differ in use, looking at real cases and docs first. Give me a comparison we can discuss, with sources I can check, within this budget. Bring back the questions most worth digging into."

**You own the goal and the judgment; it owns the research and the doing.** Look at a first round of real results before deciding where to go deeper. You will find more that way than by scripting every step up front.

### Small things right away, big things to a specialist team

Quick questions, a paragraph to rewrite, a number to crunch, a clip to trim — just ask in the conversation.

Work that takes many steps goes into Cowork. Work that benefits from a specialist method and canvas goes to the matching Pack:

- **Checking one figure?** Just ask. **Tracing where a claim really comes from?** Use Content Research.
- **One summary of a table?** Just ask. **Joining several tables and slicing them again and again?** Use Data Studio.
- **Cutting one segment?** Just ask. **Restructuring the story, fixing captions, adding charts?** Use Video Editor.

### When other people's private details are involved, turn on Auto privacy

Contracts, client files, medical records, staff lists: you want AI's help, but you don't want to hand other people's names, phone numbers and ID numbers to a cloud model.

When you start a new Cowork task, switch on **Auto privacy** next to the input box. Before anything goes to the cloud model, names, phone numbers, ID numbers, addresses and similar details are replaced with placeholders. What you see in the app, and the files it writes, still use the real values.

Put your own company, client names and internal project code names under **Always mask** in Settings; put words that keep being mistaken for names under **Never mask**. Before sending, you can also click a single word in the input box to change whether it is masked.

Tasks with Auto privacy on are left out of memory, and the switch locks once the first message is sent. Text inside images is not masked; the app marks such images as "Image content is not masked". If the on-device recognition model isn't available yet, DeTars masks using your word lists and pattern rules, and tells you which kinds of details might slip through.

## 2. Grow scattered notes into a knowledge base that lasts for years

The books you read, the clients you talk to, the projects you finish — each teaches you something, and a few months later most of it has faded.

Let DeTars organise them into your own notes and knowledge base, link them up, and bring them back when something similar comes along:

> "Put the three things most worth keeping from this project into my notes, and link them to what I wrote before about customer interviews."
>
> "Go through my past supplier comparisons. Which criteria still apply this time?"

Notes are plain Markdown files on your own computer. You can open them, edit them and take them anywhere.

## 3. The longer you work together, the better it knows you

DeTars remembers from each piece of work who you are, what you care about and how things got done, so you don't have to explain everything again.

If it remembers something wrong, or you've changed your mind, just say so:

> "My preference has changed. Please update the old record and tell me where it applies."

**Things you've done a few times can become ready-made methods.** For approaches that keep coming up, DeTars suggests turning them into a Skill or a small tool. You can also ask directly:

> "Look through these tasks. Which steps are worth turning into a Skill or a tool? Pick the most useful one and use it next time."

Weekly report templates, proposal structures and review checklists all make good Skills. Attach one to a project and related work will follow it automatically.

Can't remember how you did something before? Just ask: "Why did we drop that approach last time?" "Have we done something like this before?" It will find the original records.

## 4. Questions worth researching over time

### Content Research: really understand a question

How a technology gets adopted, what is changing in an industry, whether a claim holds up — it follows the trail back to original sources such as interviews, podcasts, videos, documents and code, and lays out the sources, the disagreements and the conclusions. You can get an insightful report or a polished long-form piece.

> "How do companies actually start using enterprise AI? Compare three typical cases first, and next time dig deeper from there."

The key insights from the research connect into a graph. When a link catches your eye, ask: "What's the evidence?" "What if that assumption changes?"

### Equity Companion: stop letting opportunities slip by

News never stops. The hard part is telling an opportunity from a trap, and remembering why you bought in the first place.

Tell it which companies you believe in, and it will lay out your reasons, the risks and the signals to watch. When news breaks, one question is enough: "Which of my reasons does this change?"

> "I'm bullish on this company. Break down my reasons, check customers, suppliers and competitors for other variables, and review it with fresh news every month. Tell me if anything changes."

Over time, looking back at your past calls shows you your own decision habits.

## 5. Turn ideas into things you can see

Every Pack has a canvas: point at something, and it picks up from there.

### AI Video: turn the picture in your head into shots

Say who it's for and what feeling you want. The director proposes a few visual directions; you pick one, and it generates, compares and assembles the shots.

> "Make a three-shot video about this product for a young audience — light and imaginative. Give me two clearly different directions first."
>
> "Keep the mood of this one and the same character, but change the action."

Generation costs money, so it confirms the specs and budget with you before starting.

### Video Editor: you do the talking, it does the editing

Hand over your footage. It cuts repetition, fixes captions, adds data cards and B-roll, and shows you a full preview first.

> "This is mainly about cost changes. Keep my voice, cut the repetition, and turn the key numbers into data cards."
>
> "This pause is too long." "This line is the point — make it stand out."

### Data Studio: let your data answer the next question

Hand it a spreadsheet or a database. It checks the fields and definitions first, then builds charts and dashboards. Click a region or a bar to ask why.

> "Find the business whose gross margin changed most this year, break it down by region and product, and put it in a dashboard."

To share it, export an offline HTML file.

### Programming: understand and change a project without knowing how to code

No need to learn programming first, or to keep project docs yourself. Hand the project to the Programming Pack and ask in plain words:

> "How does this feature work?"
>
> "If I change this, what else is affected?"

It finds the relevant code, works out how the parts connect, and explains the impact and options in words you understand. Start by understanding; over time you can take part in design, changes and testing.

### Long Novel Studio: write a long novel with an editorial team

Put the world, the characters' relationships and the core mystery into a project, then move forward chapter by chapter. One editor watches continuity, another reads as your audience, and the chief editor brings it together.

> "First set up the relationships and the mystery for volume one, then write chapter one."

Select a passage in the reading canvas to discuss point of view, pacing and motivation. Chapters, settings and outlines are all Markdown, so the more you write, the easier it is to look back and revise.

### Destiny Companion: people need to believe in fate

However far technology goes, fate remains a mystery. The Destiny Companion draws on Eastern and Western divination — tarot, Zi Wei astrology and the I Ching — to help you see what's on your mind more clearly.

> "What's my lucky colour tomorrow?"
>
> "Are he and I a good match?"

Tap a card or a palace in the observatory to keep asking about the same reading. Readings from important moments are kept, so later you can look back on a record of yourself and of time.

### Summon: give a character their own time and world

Describe who they are, what your relationship is, and where their story has reached. A setup colleague helps bring the character to life. Then talk with them directly on the character stage; their look and voice can be added along the way.

> "Keep him at the end of chapter three. I'm an old friend he hasn't seen in years. Let's start with the reunion."

### One big job, several teams in relay

Want to turn a complex piece of research into a two-minute video? The lead asks Content Research to check numbers and find sources, AI Video to make a concept shot, and Video Editor to cut it together.

> "Turn this research and my recorded footage into a two-minute video. Source the key numbers and explain the abstract idea with one generated shot. Bring in the right colleagues and hand me the finished result."

## 6. Let go gradually, and keep your attention for what matters

As projects pile up, hand them to the Chief of Staff. It is on by default: it knows when a task is waiting for you, finished or newly started, and when you're away from your computer it can reach you through IM apps such as Feishu or Telegram.

> "Look after these projects for me. Keep them moving toward their goals, and come to me together when there are results or decisions only I can make."

The Chief of Staff learns your way of thinking from the guidance you give it. It also reviews what DeTars remembers on a regular basis and helps you correct anything that's wrong.

For especially complex tasks that tend to go in circles, click the bell at the top and shorten the reminder interval so the Chief of Staff checks in sooner.

### Can't look at the screen? Have replies read aloud

Turn on **Voice replies** next to the input box: the text arrives first and the spoken version follows. Choose "Always", or "When I speak" so it answers by voice only when you speak to it. In Settings you can pick a voice and set a length above which it sends text only (300 characters by default).

> "Change Chat's voice replies to 'When I speak', and send text only above 500 characters."

In channels with voice messages, such as Feishu and Telegram, you get a voice message. Slack and Teams receive an audio file. LINE and Zalo currently get text only. You can always replay it in the app.

**Start with one goal, and carry the results, knowledge and methods into the next. The longer you use it, the more you own.**

documents.title: When DeTars gets stuck: keep your progress, take another route
documents.markdown:
# When DeTars gets stuck: keep your progress, take another route

When work hits an obstacle, ask the model to look at what's actually happening, find another way, and keep what's already done. The point is how this piece of work gets finished.

## 1. First, secure the work

Tell the model what you were doing, which step it stopped at, and any message you saw. Have it check the original task, the existing files and anything still running, and save whatever usable results there are.

> "This task stopped here. First check what's already done and whether the original operation is still running, keep the current version, then decide how to continue."

For long tasks, leave a short handoff: the goal, where the materials are, what's been decided, the current version and the next step. Whether you continue the original task, switch models or ask another assistant to take over, everyone starts from a clear point.

## 2. Pick the next route for the situation

### The model is responding oddly

Check the current model, the service status and any account messages. If you need to sign in again, do it in the window shown. If the service is busy, look at the task's state and choose to wait, resume, or switch to another suitable model.

Save your progress before switching; afterwards, check what material the new model received and what has been done so far.

> "Keep the progress so far. Find out what went wrong with the current model, then give me a good option for continuing this work."

### A web page or source can't be reached

Try the original source, a browser that's already signed in, a page reader, a download or a transcript. If a sign-in, QR scan or verification is needed, complete it in the real window and the model continues from the same page.

Describe the goal as "get this material" or "verify this fact", and the model can choose tools and routes around that purpose.

### File handling, a tool or a generation job is stuck

Have the model check the task's state, the output folder and the error message. File conversion, command-line tools, code or any other available capability can be a way to finish the job. For downloads and generation jobs already under way, check their progress before deciding what to do next.

> "Look at the original task and the existing files. Finish this step with whatever works now, and build on what's already done."

For external generation or paid services, look at the query results, the files already produced and the billing status together.

### Messages aren't getting through a channel

Check the target account, the connection state and the channel's messages. If the model has a tool for it, it can look at the actual state first, then handle starting or pairing. Any sign-in you need to complete yourself comes with a link to the right place.

### The app or a settings page isn't working

First confirm which installation and data folder are in use, and protect your project files and configuration. A local assistant outside the app can help check. If the evidence points to configuration, model routing or task bindings, use the offline repair manual below.

## 3. Combine the capabilities you have

You can ask the model to use existing Skills, file tools, the browser, the command line, Python or JavaScript, or to hand a well-defined subtask to an external CLI assistant on your computer.

> "Look for existing tools and Skills for this goal. If another approach is needed, explain why and carry on within what I've already asked."

Be clear about what must be kept, which formats are acceptable, and the time or cost limits, and the model can weigh the routes more easily. When it needs more material or a decision from you, have it ask only the question that really affects the next step.

## 4. Outside the app, there's an offline repair route

`detars-rescue` is a Markdown manual that a local assistant can read. It covers problems with configuration, model routing and task bindings.

While the app works, ask the model to find it among the local Skills. For offline repair, take `detars-rescue` from the actual installation, or use a saved copy of `OFFLINE-RESCUE.md`, and give it to an assistant with access to your local files. If you need a copy, ask a maintainer for one that matches your installation.

A repair centres on one clear goal: confirm the installation and the fault, keep a private byte-for-byte backup of the original, then make the smallest fix. Before writing anything offline, make sure the app and any related processes have fully quit. To verify, check the files, then startup, then the original feature, and leave a way to roll back.

You can put it like this:

> "Please check this installation using the offline rescue manual. First confirm the target, the error and the proposed change, keep a backup, and then fix it within what I've asked. Report back the actual result, how far verification got, and how to roll back."

## 5. Make it easy for whoever takes over

A good handoff only needs this:

- **What needs to be done**: the goal and the important constraints.
- **What already exists**: materials, results, the current version, and anything still running.
- **Where it's stuck**: the original message, when it happened and where; remove keys and private content before sharing.
- **What's been tried**: what was actually done and what verification showed.
- **What happens next**: how to continue, who needs to help, and where the backups and rollback are.

**Let what's in front of you decide the route, and keep the results in your hands. Carry on where you can; when you need another route, take your progress with you.**

---
name: provider-accounts
description: Check the user's hosted AI provider account — remaining balance, credits, free quota or resource packs, plan quota, token/request usage, billing, top-up and sign-in — for Volcengine Ark/BytePlus, MiniMax, Alibaba Bailian/DashScope, fal, Runway, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Moonshot/Kimi, OpenRouter, ElevenLabs, Z.ai and models they host. Use when the user asks 额度、余额、还剩多少、还剩多少 token、用了多少、花了多少钱、账单、套餐、充值、开通、登录账号. Not for a DeTars Pack's own generation allowance (use that Pack's budget operation).
---

# Provider accounts

Answer an account question with the provider's own numbers. Work through the
four steps below, reading only the reference for the provider you need.

## 1. Which account

Take the provider id, base URL host and region from the current DeTars setup
(runtime facts, or the route a tool actually used), not from the model brand.

- A `byteplus` route whose host is `ark.cn-beijing.volces.com` is a Volcengine
  China account.
- minimaxi.com and minimax.io, moonshot.cn and kimi.ai, and Bailian Beijing and
  international are separate accounts with separate keys.
- A model served through fal, together or vydra is billed by that host, not by
  the model's brand.

## 2. Which number

These are separate pools. Report each one under its own name; never add them up.

| Pool | Example |
|---|---|
| DeTars Pack allowance | aivideo `budget` "remaining 1": DeTars's own count, not money |
| Plan quota | Ark Agent/Coding Plan, MiniMax Token Plan, Bailian Token Plan |
| Pay-as-you-go balance / credits | Ark account balance, DeepSeek balance, fal credits |
| Free quota / resource packs | Ark free quota per model |
| Usage (tokens / requests) | delayed aggregates (Ark: 5–30 min) |
| Billing (money owed) | usually settled the next day |

The `usage` returned by one generation is what that call consumed, not what is
left.

## 3. Which identity

| Kind | Providers | How |
|---|---|---|
| Same inference key | MiniMax, Runway, DeepSeek, Moonshot, OpenRouter `/key`, Z.ai; ElevenLabs likely (permission scope not verified) | Reuse the key DeTars already holds, without reading it: `detars infer provider exec --provider <id> --env <VAR> -- <command>`. The child reads the key from that environment variable. |
| Separate sign-in | Ark (`arkcli auth login`), Bailian (`bl auth login --console`) | Run the vendor CLI login yourself; it opens a browser or prints a link |
| Specific account permission | fal `billing:usage:read` (included in BILLING, READONLY and FULL key presets) | Reuse the configured key through `detars infer provider exec` if it has that permission; otherwise open the key settings for the user |
| Admin / management key | OpenAI admin key, OpenRouter `/credits` | Tell the user which console page creates it and where to put it; never ask them to paste a key into chat |
| Console only | Google, Replicate, Kling direct | Open the console with the browser tool (try `import_signins` first) |

When a reference says a query needs a separate identity, don't retry with the
inference key. An auth error there is expected, not a sign of a broken key.

Do not read vendor credential or configuration files (for example `~/.arkcli/`
or `~/.volc/`) to extract keys, and never put a literal key in a command. For
same-key queries, use `detars infer provider exec`; the child script reads the
injected environment variable without printing it.

Some vendor CLIs ship or install official agent Skills: arkcli, mmx and bl,
plus Runway's skills. Follow the provider reference's install/init step, then
check where the Skills were installed and read the relevant one by its absolute
path for detail. Installing can also write into the
user's other agents' skill folders (arkcli writes `~/.agents/skills` and
`~/.claude/skills`). Mention that in your reply.

## 4. Reply for a non-technical user

- Lead with the numbers: pool name, amount, unit, as-of time and any delay.
- When a sign-in is needed, start it yourself and ask for exactly one action,
  for example: "我已打开火山登录页，请在弹出的窗口扫码 / 点确认，好了回我一句".
  Give a raw command only if the user asked for one, or every automatic path
  failed.
- Say what you could not see and why, for example "账单要明天才出".

## References

Each file starts with the date it was last checked against official sources.

- [Volcengine Ark](references/ark.md), including `byteplus` routes on China hosts
- [BytePlus ModelArk international](references/byteplus.md)
- [MiniMax](references/minimax.md)

# Volcengine Ark (火山方舟)

Checked 2026-10-20 against arkcli 1.0.40 (`arkcli usage balance --help`) and its
official skills `arkcli-usage`, `arkcli-billing` and `arkcli-auth`.

Applies to DeTars provider `volcengine`, and to a `byteplus` route whose host is
`ark.cn-beijing.volces.com` (a China account despite the id).

## Identity: control plane, not ARK_API_KEY

Balance, usage and billing go through the control plane. They need a
Volcengine sign-in (SSO, giving STS credentials). `ARK_API_KEY` and arkcli's
`--api-key` only cover inference. The AK/SK login channel is closed in arkcli
1.0.40.

The supported balance and usage queries below use the control plane, not the
Ark inference host. Do not guess balance or usage paths on that inference host
or probe them with `ARK_API_KEY`.

- Install: `npm i -g @volcengine/ark-cli` (or run once through
  `npx --yes @volcengine/ark-cli <args>`). Its postinstall runs
  `arkcli +connect --refresh`, which installs about 26 official `arkcli-*`
  Skills into `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.claude/skills`. Tell the user.
- Check: `arkcli auth status`. "not configured" means no sign-in yet.
- Sign in from an agent (non-TTY), two steps:
  1. `arkcli auth login --no-browser` prints JSON with `authorize_url`. Open that
     URL for the user, in the browser tool or by handing it over. They sign in on
     any device and copy the base64 code the page shows.
  2. `arkcli auth login --no-browser --code <code>` finishes the login.
  Both flags belong to `auth login` itself, not to `volc-sso`. If `ve` (volcengine
  CLI ≥ 1.0.45) is already logged in, an interactive `arkcli auth login` can
  reuse that session.

## Queries

| Question | Command | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Free quota / resource packs left | `arkcli usage balance --type free-quota [--modality LLM\|ComputerVision\|Audio\|Embedding\|Router] [--model <name>] --format json` | Video models are `ComputerVision`; `--modality` takes no aliases |
| Agent / Coding Plan quota | `arkcli usage balance --type plan [--product agent-plan\|coding-plan\|agent-plan-team\|coding-plan-team]` | Same data as `arkcli usage plan` |
| Media asset library capacity | `arkcli usage balance --type media-asset` | |
| Tokens / requests used | `arkcli usage stats --start <YYYY-MM-DD> --mine` | 5–30 min delay; read `arkcli-usage/references/arkcli-usage-stats.md` first. A root account has no sub-user identity: drop `--mine` when it says so |
| Money actually owed | `arkcli billing list --start <YYYY-MM>` | Settled T+1; read `arkcli-billing` first. Needs split billing enabled on the account; otherwise say so and point to the console's billing center |

The account's CNY cash balance is not exposed by arkcli 1.0.40 (there is no
`billing balance`); for that, open the console's billing center. A free-quota row
in state `Unavailable` means the model is not activated yet, not that its quota
is used up.

Each official skill says to read its reference before running these commands.
Do that once the CLI is installed. Speech models (TTS/ASR) have no usage or
balance query in arkcli.

Console for humans: <https://console.volcengine.com/ark/region:cn-beijing/overview>

# Alibaba Bailian / DashScope (阿里云百炼)

Checked 2026-10-20 against `modelstudioai/cli` (npm `bailian-cli` 2.4.0; README and
`packages/commands/src/commands/usage/*.ts`).

DeTars providers `qwen` and `alibaba` (env `QWEN_API_KEY`, `MODELSTUDIO_API_KEY`,
`DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`).

## Identity: console sign-in, not the API key

Every `bl usage` command needs a console OAuth sign-in. An API key
(`bl auth login --api-key`) does not cover usage queries. AK/SK is only needed for
Token Plan seat administration.

- Sign in: `bl auth login --console`; international accounts add
  `--console-site international`. It opens a browser sign-in; the user only
  confirms there.
- `bl skill init` installs Bailian's official Skills. The official installer also
  installs them automatically. Tell the user.

## Queries

| Question | Command |
|---|---|
| Free quota per model | `bl usage free [--model <name>]` |
| Usage summary | `bl usage summary` |
| Usage statistics | `bl usage stats` |
| Token Plan quota | `bl usage token-plan` |
| Coding Plan quota | `bl usage coding-plan` |

Beijing and international are separate accounts.

# BytePlus ModelArk (international)

Checked 2026-10-20. Not verified: an account balance or usage API, and an
international arkcli build. The arkcli checked here is the China build
(`arkcli-volc`).

- First confirm the host. A DeTars `byteplus` route on `ark.cn-beijing.volces.com`
  is a Volcengine China account; use [ark](ark.md).

# MiniMax

Checked 2026-10-20 against MiniMax's official CLI `mmx-cli` source (MiniMax-AI/cli
@a965e72: `src/client/endpoints.ts`, `src/commands/quota/show.ts`) and OpenClaw's
`provider-usage.fetch.minimax.ts`.

Inference key env: `MINIMAX_API_KEY`.

## Identity: same key

The inference key works (Bearer). Regions are separate accounts: mmx uses
`https://api.minimax.io` (global) and `https://api.minimax.cn` (cn). Use the host
DeTars's minimax provider actually uses.

## Two pools, picked by key type

| Key | Endpoint (relative to the base host) | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| Pay-as-you-go secret key (`sk-api-…`) | `GET /account/query_balance` | available / cash / voucher / credit / owed balance |
| Token / Coding Plan key or portal OAuth | `GET /v1/token_plan/remains` | per-model plan remains |

Report the two pools separately.

## Ways to run it

- With the DeTars key, write a small HTTP script that reads `MINIMAX_API_KEY`
  from its environment, and run it as
  `detars infer provider exec --provider minimax --env MINIMAX_API_KEY -- python3 <script>`.
  `mmx` reads its key from `--api-key` or its own config file, not from that
  environment variable at query time. Don't put the key in argv.
- If the user already set up `mmx` (`npm i -g mmx-cli`, then `mmx auth login`),
  `mmx quota show` does the same selection. The CLI ships an official skill
  (`skill/SKILL.md`); `MiniMax-AI/skills` has more.
